body.statement: Does the support-scoped compiler handle yield a finite do-search calculus that is sound and complete for \(\tau_{x,y}\) over \(\Theta_S\), permits signed intermediate expressions without invalid cancellation, and normalizes every successful derivation to a bounded certificate \(\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) whose denominators divide \(D_S(P)\)? Establish termination, rule-by-rule soundness, completeness relative to the tensor criterion, and an explicit certificate-size bound, or exhibit the first finite counterexample.
body.justification: The unresolved content is whether product-preserving signed search rules can realize the complete semantic criterion without materializing the full response tensor.
body.gap: Do-search inherits completeness only from its underlying calculus, and positivity-aware work does not compile structural-zero gains into tensor-normal certificates.
body.consumer: A positive answer gives a support-aware extension of do-search with independently checkable success and failure receipts.

obligation.what_is_open: A finite syntax of do-search states and an explicit list of signed, support-scoped transition rules whose derivations normalize to the tensor certificate, together with a simulation of every tensor row-space elimination by those rules.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen compiler handle specifies semantic invariants and a desired normalization but does not define a transition relation, rule side conditions, expression encoding, or cancellation discipline. Consequently termination and rule-by-rule soundness are not well-typed properties of the present handle, and neither a completeness proof nor a finite counterexample to an unspecified calculus can be given.
obligation.attempted: The support-saturated response sets, positive-prefix district signatures, commuting rootwise row-space projections, rational Gaussian elimination, and signed tensor identity were compiled into a finite semantic decision procedure. What remains is a bidirectional simulation between a concrete do-search grammar and these tensor operations; in particular, signed products of district signatures must retain intervention scopes through cancellation.
obligation.partial_result: The semantic tensor compiler is finite and complete: let \(K=(|S|+1)^m\), \(M=|T(S)|\), and \(r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\).  Enumeration of the finite sets \(T_j(S)\), formation of \(B\), and rational Gaussian elimination decide whether \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\in\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\).  On success, one may choose \(r\) independent rows and a nonsingular \(r\)-by-\(r\) minor, obtaining a certificate \(\lambda\) with at most \(r\le\min\{K,M\}\) nonzero entries.  Cramer's rule and Hadamard's inequality bound the numerator and denominator of each reduced coefficient by \(r^{r/2}\), hence its bit length by \(O(r\log r)\).  The resulting functional has denominator dividing \(D_S(P)\).  On failure, the one-district rational perturbation in the rational-interior-twins theorem is a finite exact nonidentification certificate.  This proves a bounded, sound, and complete response-tensor decision procedure, but it does not prove that a specified do-search transition system realizes that procedure without materializing the tensor.
